entries.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
entries.summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity.
entries.why: Balances representation quality and generation speed in discrete autoregressive image models.

entries.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
entries.summary: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control.
entries.why: Advances joint perspective and BEV video generation for reactive driving world models.

entries.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
entries.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead.
entries.why: Analyzes the design, simplification, and stability of Hyper-Connections in large models.

entries.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
entries.summary: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget.…
entries.why: Examines whether to spend inference budgets on weight precision or option-order averaging.
